overall: The AG found neither the Board nor the Police Chief Search Committee violated the Open Meeting Law on any of the three allegations: committee composition, executive session purpose statements, and the private interviews.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the seven-member preliminary screening committee was improper because a committee must have fewer than a quorum of the three-member parent Board.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Search Committee's composition was valid.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Search Committee did not state its executive session purpose at five spring 2012 meetings (March 29 through May 10).
allegations.key_passage: we credit the Chair's assertion that he stated the executive session purpose before entering into executive session at each meeting and find no violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged all candidate interviews were held in executive session and the Town Administrator re-interviewed them privately, so no candidate was interviewed in open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Search Committee followed the law by meeting in executive session only during the preliminary screening stage, and recommending to the Board a list of candidates it deemed qualified for further consideration.
